title: Terraform conductor for EKS master fleet bootstrap and health orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reusable, idempotent Terraform 'conductor' module that composes existing lower-level pieces to bootstrap the EKS master fleet used by Redwood Private control planes. This ticket covers the module API, preflight validations, cross-account KMS/S3 state handling, upgrade-time health gating, and a safe canary rollout path for customers using VPC/private deployments. The intent is not to replace low-level modules but to provide a single opinionated orchestration layer that: 1) validates cluster prerequisites, 2) performs deterministic sequencing for control plane resources (IAM roles, KMS key policies, ECR access, control-plane workers), 3) wires in health probes and automated rollback hooks for failed upgrades, and 4) exposes observability outputs to the Console. Key constraints: must support both customer-owned state (S3+Dynamo state locking across accounts) and Redwood-managed state, be compatible with terraform >=1.6, and not require runtime imperative scripting outside Terraform long-running applies.
acceptance_criteria: Module published to internal registry with semantic version and docs page
Module performs preflight checks and fails apply with actionable errors if VPC/route table/KMS policies are misconfigured
Bootstrap sequence is idempotent: repeated apply after partial failure converges without manual cleanup
Supports customer-owned state bucket with cross-account KMS encryption and proper S3 lock lifecycle
Upgrade path uses staged canary: 5% of control planes on new revision, automated health gating prevents wider rollout on failures
Exposes outputs for Console: controlplane_endpoint, kms_key_arn, boot_time_seconds, last_successful_apply_time
Automated integration tests run in CI and pass against a small canary AWS account
implementation_notes: Design module as a thin orchestration layer that calls into: network module, iam module, kms module, eks-controlplane module
Use explicit 'phase' resources (null_resource + local-exec avoided) — prefer terraform providers/hooks where available
State: support optional variables for s3_bucket, dynamodb_table, state_kms_key. When not provided, module will create resources using naming conventions and tag ownership
Idempotency: use lifecycle 'replace_triggered_by' minimally and prefer 'create_before_destroy' for IAM role changes
Preflight: implement data sources to verify route table CIDR overlaps, ENI quotas, and existing SG rules that conflict with our bastion/endpoint patterns
Cross-account: include example role assumption configuration and recommended trust policy snippet in docs
Health gating: add a terraform-managed manifest that registers a 'bootstrap-health' marker in the Console via the API (see attachments) so that rollout automation can read health signals
Avoid storing secrets in plain-text outputs; return ARNs only and reference KMS-encrypted secrets in downstream modules
testing_plan: Unit/plan-time tests: terraform-compliance checks for must-have tags and IAM least-privilege assertions
Integration: run full apply/destroy in isolated dev account using CI pipeline, validate idempotency by interrupting apply then re-running
Canary: deploy module to a single internal customer-like account and run synthetic workloads to validate KV cache performance and API reachability
Chaos: run kubelet/etcd simulated failure scenarios during upgrade to validate rollback hooks
E2E automation will assert Console metrics presence for boot_time_seconds and last_successful_apply_time
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal dev): land RFC + module alpha in 'registry/internal' and smoke test in CI
Phase 1 (internal canary): enable for 1 internal customer cluster via engineering-oncall, monitor for 72h
Phase 2 (external opt-in): offer module to select customers with SOC/enterprise needs; require signed runbook
Phase 3 (GA): publish public docs, add to onboarding templates and update Console provisioning flows
Rollback strategy: if health gating fails, automated policy triggers terraform apply using previous module version and notifies oncall via PagerDuty
observability: Emit structured logs to logging pipeline during apply (apply-start/apply-complete/errors)
Console integration: expose module outputs as provisioning metadata so Console can plot successful boot rates and median boot time
Add tracing metadata for each apply (request id, commit sha, operator) to link terraform runs to Console traces
Metric alerts: increase in boot_time_seconds > 2x baseline or >10% failure rate triggers P1 alert
risks: Cross-account state introduces subtle KMS policy and S3 replication edge cases — mitigated by recommended trust snippets and integration tests
Terraform provider changes (AWS/EKS) could break orchestration sequencing — mitigate with pinned provider versions and CI matrix
Automating rollbacks via Terraform can be slow; need guardrails to avoid thrashing — implement health gating and rate limits
Customer environments with heavy resource drift may cause prolonged applies; increase timeouts and provide clear remediation steps
